title: Add User, UserSession, Companion tables and user_id/companion_id foreign keys to chatbot/db/models.py
description:
Modify chatbot/db/models.py to integrate the auth and companion table definitions as SQLAlchemy declarative models (User, UserSession, Companion) and add user_id and companion_id foreign key columns to existing Session and ChatMessage tables.

Before editing, inspect:
- AGENTS.md
- docs/plans_tasks.md
- docs/operations.md
- docs/architecture.md
- docs/PLANS/ACTIVE/CHATBOT/README.md
- docs/PLANS/ACTIVE/CHATBOT/DISPATCH.md
- chatbot/db/models.py (existing database models — understand SQLAlchemy base class, column conventions, existing table names, session model class name, chat message model class name, and any existing foreign key patterns)
- chatbot/auth/models.py (created by task c.1 — AUTH_MODEL_DEFINITIONS dict)
- chatbot/companions/companion.py (created by task c.3 — COMPANION_MODEL_DEFINITIONS dict)

Do not infer APIs, constructor signatures, function names, module locations, or service topology from the task description alone. Inspect the referenced documents and existing implementation files first, then implement against the actual repository.

STRICT FILE SCOPE: Create or modify ONLY chatbot/db/models.py. Do NOT modify any other file under any circumstance. Do NOT update documentation, READMEs, operations guides, or any code outside the listed path. If you believe other files need updating, ignore that impulse and finish the task with only the listed file modified. Out-of-scope edits will cause the task to be rejected.

Implementation details:

1. Open chatbot/db/models.py and understand:
   - The SQLAlchemy declarative base class (likely Base = declarative_base() or similar).
   - Column naming conventions: snake_case vs CamelCase, column types, default values.
   - Existing model class names — the session model class name and chat message model class name must not be renamed.
   - The import style for SQLAlchemy imports (from sqlalchemy import ... or import sqlalchemy as sa).
   - Any existing __all__ or module exports.

2. Add three new SQLAlchemy declarative model classes:
   - `User`: columns per AUTH_MODEL_DEFINITIONS['users'], with __tablename__ = 'users'.
   - `UserSession`: columns per AUTH_MODEL_DEFINITIONS['user_sessions'], with __tablename__ = 'user_sessions'. Include ForeignKey on user_id referencing users.user_id.
   - `Companion`: columns per COMPANION_MODEL_DEFINITIONS['companions'], with __tablename__ = 'companions'. Include ForeignKey on user_id referencing users.user_id.

3. Extend the existing session model (whatever it is named — Session, ConversationSession, etc.):
   - Add column `user_id` (String(36), ForeignKey('users.user_id'), nullable=True, index=True).
   - Add column `companion_id` (String(36), ForeignKey('companions.companion_id'), nullable=True, index=True).
   - Add relationship() backrefs if the existing code pattern uses relationships.

4. Extend the existing chat message/turn model (whatever it is named — ChatMessage, Turn, Message, etc.):
   - Add column `user_id` (String(36), ForeignKey('users.user_id'), nullable=True, index=True).
   - Add column `companion_id` (String(36), ForeignKey('companions.companion_id'), nullable=True, index=True).
   - Add relationship() backrefs if the existing code pattern uses relationships.

5. Do NOT remove, rename, or retype any existing column on any existing table. All existing columns must remain exactly as they are. The pgvector embedding column (if present) must not be touched.

6. All new FK columns must be nullable to avoid breaking existing rows that have no user or companion assignment.
